guarantees.claim: When rst_ni is low (reset active), data_in_prev_q is cleared to all zeros.
When not in reset and data_in_prev_we equals SP2V_HIGH, data_in_prev_q is updated with data_in_prev_d.
When not in reset and data_in_prev_we is not equal to SP2V_HIGH, data_in_prev_q retains its previous value (implicit hold).

assumptions.claim: External logic must assert rst_ni low for at least one clock edge to guarantee data_in_prev_q is cleared to zero.
assumptions.cond: during power-up or any reset event
assumptions.risk: If rst_ni never asserts low, data_in_prev_q may contain undefined or residual data, potentially leaking previous state.

assumptions.claim: data_in_prev_d must be valid and stable at the rising clock edge when data_in_prev_we equals SP2V_HIGH.
assumptions.risk: Capturing unstable or invalid data can corrupt data_in_prev_q, causing downstream functional errors.

uncertain_points.claim: If data_in_prev_we is a multi-bit signal and SP2V_HIGH is not a single high value, any non-SP2V_HIGH value causes hold; need to confirm that SP2V_HIGH defines the sole active level and that no other legal values should trigger an update.
uncertain_points.cond: unknown: depends on definition of SP2V_HIGH and width of data_in_prev_we
uncertain_points.risk: If other values were intended to cause an update, they would be silently ignored, possibly leading to missed data.

uncertain_points.claim: Downstream logic that reads data_in_prev_q may depend on its reset value being zero; need to verify that all consumers can tolerate a non-zero random value if reset is not asserted.
uncertain_points.risk: Unreset data_in_prev_q could propagate as valid data, causing incorrect operation or security exposure.
